hypotheses.justification: The bound can be proved for arbitrary real C, with a different constant. Only finitely many primes have 1 + C/p ≤ 0; handle these exceptional factors separately, and bound the remaining positive factors raised to r by nonnegative local weights whose excess over 1 is O(1/p). Their excess divided by p is summable, so `divisor_product_mean` gives a bound proportional to U. Negative bases in `Real.rpow` have magnitude at most the corresponding absolute-value power, and zero factors can be handled separately. Thus nonnegativity of C is not needed.
